title: BH-Exit: Label-Free Early Termination for HNSW Search via Bucket-Histogram Stability

contributions.purpose: Enable label-free early termination of HNSW search that detects convergence earlier than exact ID matching.
contributions.mechanism: BH-Exit monitors bucket-histogram stability: corpus vectors are assigned to buckets via offline k-means clustering, and search terminates when the L1 distance between consecutive bucket histograms falls below a threshold.
contributions.evaluation: Coarse-grained monitoring that ignores within-bucket churn, enabling earlier convergence detection than ID-Overlap.
contributions.domain: approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) / HNSW dense retrieval search
contributions.source_quote: We propose BH-Exit, a label-free early termination method for HNSW search that monitors bucket-histogram stability via k-means clustering.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate latency improvement over the ID-Overlap baseline without quality loss.
contributions.mechanism: Replacing exact ID-Overlap monitoring with bucket-histogram stability monitoring.
contributions.evaluation: 28.0% p50 latency improvement over ID-Overlap on BEIR TREC-COVID while maintaining equivalent retrieval quality (nDCG@10 = 0.6725).
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate 28.0% p50 latency improvement over ID-Overlap on BEIR TREC-COVID while maintaining equivalent retrieval quality (nDCG@10 = 0.6725).

contributions.purpose: Validate that semantic clustering (not random bucketing) drives the gains.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation comparing k-means semantic bucket assignment against random assignment.
contributions.evaluation: Semantic bucket assignment via k-means outperforms random assignment by 31.3% in expansion savings.
contributions.source_quote: We validate that semantic bucket assignment via k-means outperforms random assignment by 31.3% in expansion savings, confirming the importance of semantic clustering.

contributions.purpose: Establish robustness of the method across bucket granularities.
contributions.mechanism: Sweeping the number of clusters/buckets C over a range.
contributions.evaluation: Robust across bucket granularities (C in [64, 4096]), with consistent improvement over ID-Overlap ranging from 13.2% to 40.5%.
contributions.source_quote: We show robustness across bucket granularities (C in [64, 4096]), with consistent improvement over ID-Overlap ranging from 13.2% to 40.5%.

self_declared_provenance.quote: The ID-Overlap method (Busolin et al. 2024; Teofili & Lin 2025) monitors the overlap between consecutive candidate sets and terminates when the overlap exceeds a threshold. However, this approach requires exact matching between candidate sets.

These methods rely on exact matching or learned predictors, whereas BH-Exit uses coarse-grained histogram stability that captures distributional convergence without requiring exact ID matching or model training.

These methods use clustering for compression and approximate distance computation, while BH-Exit uses clustering for convergence detection - a fundamentally different application of the same underlying technique.
